case_source: (Form the judgment and Order dated 1st December 2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No 2218 of 2004.)
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J: The defendant- petitioners seek leave to appeal against the impugned judgment and order dated 1st December, 2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2218 of 2004 discharging the rule issued upon the respondent No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 26.02.2001 of the Assistant Judge, Rajapur in Title Suit No. 63 of 1999 under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act decreeing the suit should not be set aside.

2. The respondent No. 1 filed the suit as the plaintiff stating, inter alia, that Ananta Kumar, Madhusudhan and Ruhhini Kumar were owners and possessors of 1.30 acres of land of S.A. Khatian No. 1354 beating plot No. 4103 of Mouza Rajapur; that Modhusudhan died leaving his cousin Ananata Kumar as his heir; that Ananta  Kumar sold 21 decimals of land to the plaintiff vide registered kabala deed dated 25.11.69 and delivered possession from the northern portion of plot No. 4103 and the plaintiff got, his name mutated and paid rents and have been possessing the suit land; that the plaintiff dug a pond from the western portion and made drain from the western portion for draining water and made a east facing road, planted different kind of trees, constructed tin shed house; that Rajapur High School has no right, title and possession in the suit land; that defendant No. 2-4 as the teachers of the said school used to reside towards the south of plot No. 4103; that the defendant No. 1 Head Master of the said school for the benefit of defendant Nos. 4 by using the name of school illegally threatened to grab the suit land for which the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous petition case No. 263 of 1999 in the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Jhalakati; that the plaintiff also made General Diary Entry No. 514 on 15.04.1999. That under the leadership of defendant No.1, the defendant forcibly dispossessed the plaintiff from .08 decimals of land described in schedule Kha to the plaint; that the defendant No. 1 in order to legalize his illegal activities of dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit land made statement in the daily Ajker Barta dated 18.04.1999 and thereafter hired some peoples, broke out and old tin shed and the reconstructed the said tin shed on the eastern portion of the land of the plaintiff and created obstacle to the access of the house of the plaintiff; the defendant No. 1 cut earth from the south east portion of the suit land and filled up the floor of the newly on strutted house and changed the nature and character of the land of the plaintiff; that defendant on 12.05.1999 started unfinished work of the newly constructed house and the plaintiff informed the matter to the police and the police issued warning notice but the defendants did not pay heed and completed the work; that the defendants caused damage to the plaintiff amounting to Taka 50,000/- by dispossessing him from the suit land. The plaintiff requested defendants to hand over the possession but refused and hence the case.

3. The defendant No. 1 filed written statement denying the material allegations stating, inter alia, that Ananta Kumar, Modhusudhan and Ruhini were the owners and possessor of the suit land and Modhusudhan transferred his entire share to Rajapur pilot High School and delivered possession in favour of the school and the said school is an old institution of 1000 years and its main building is situated on 9.30 acres of land; that the school possessing the suit land for more than 50 years and Modhushudhan is a life member of the school; that vocational branch of the school is situated on the suit land and there are trees of different kinds in the land; that during liberation war all the documents were lost and the then Headmaster died and taking advantage the plaintiff created a forged and fraudulent deed and claimed the suit land; the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous petition Case No. 263 of 1999 and there was enquiry and possession of the defendant was found by the enquiry officer and Miscellaneous petition was dismissed on 05.08.1999. The plaintiff took a Criminal Revision before the Sessions Judge which is pending. The plaintiff filed the case falsely and as such the same is liable to be dismissed.

4. The suit was decreed and thereafter defendant No.1 on misconception of law filed Title Appeal No. 42 of 2001 and thereafter having realized that an appeal has been filed wrongly, filed Civil Revision No. 3161 of 2001 against the order dated 30.4.2001 praying for continuing with the stay order of the impugned judgment and decree which was passed by the District Judge, Jhalakati in Title Appeal No.42 of 2001.Upon hearing the revision, the rule was discharged.

5. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the petitioner as per order passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 468 of 2004 mentioned the matter before the High Court Division on 22.05.2004 and the civil revisional application came up in the list on 23.05.2004 as in and had been in the list but could not be taken up, not for the fault of the petitioner but for other reasons and when the matter was taken up for hearing the plaintiff respondent raised objection and the petitioner by swearing supplementary affidavit brought the entire fact before the High Court Division and the. Court found that there was no latches on the part of the petitioner and the High Court Division after hearing both the parties issued rule on 30.06.2004. But the Single Judge of the High Court Division misappropriated those facts and thereby erred in law in discharging the Rule.

<u>6. It appears that the suit under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act at the instance of the respondent No.1 was decreed against which an incompetent appeal was filed. Thereafter, the appellate Court held that an appeal does not lie whereupon the defendant filed revisional application with an application for condonation of delay and the delay in filing the revisional application was condoned, against which the plaintiff moved Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 468 of 2004 and this Court by order dated 22.05.2004 give direction to the defendant petitioners to move the said revisional application before the High Court Division for disposal positively by 26th of May, 2004, in default, the said revisional application shall stand rejected as barred by limitation. It appears that the defendant thereupon mentioned the matter for hearing and the same was listed on 24.05.2004, 25.05.2004 and 26.05.2004 but did not get the matter heard as directed by this Court. Again the matter was listed after a lapse of one month on 23.06.2004 and lastly on 30.06.2004 the rule was issued along with the ad-interim order of stay. It appears that pursuant to the order of this Court the defendant petitioners did not take any positive steps for getting the revisional application heard by the High Court Division by 26th of May 2004 and consequently pursuant to this Courts order dated 22.05.2004 the revisional application stood rejected on 26.05.2004 as barred by limitation.</u>

7. In view of the above, we do not find any substance in the submission of learned Counsel for the petitioners and the rule issued on 30.06.2004 along with ad-interim order of stay was passed at a time in the revisional application when the matter had already stood rejected as barred by limitation pursuant to the order of this Court dated 22. 05. 2004 passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 468 of 2004.

8. This petition is, accordingly, dismissed.

End.
